title: Pilot Ops Fastlane — Cheat Sheet (Compact Draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, field-ready cheat sheet for SEs and Ops partners running inference pilot engagements. Focus: get to a safe, measurable pilot in 72 hours with clear rollbacks, cost controls, and an ops escalation path.

Audience:
- Sales Engineers (SEs) running the initial pilot call
- Platform/Customer Ops engineers executing the pilot setup
- Solutions Engineers supporting canary policies and SLA comms

TL;DR (1 line):
Ship a low-friction pilot that proves latency and cost predictability while preserving easy fallbacks — enable confident decision to commit to Dedicated or Private.

3-minute demo / demo flow (speaker notes):
1) Setup (30s) — explain the two pilot modes we’ll demo: hosted quick-embed (fast) vs reserved pilot node (predictable).
   - Script: "We’ll run the same prompt set on both so you can see latency and per-token variance; then toggle routing to show fallback behavior."
2) Run sample requests (60s) — show streaming generation, token-level cost meter, and console latency histogram.
   - Speaker cue: highlight the console’s per-route token breakdown and the ability to pin model versions.
3) Failure simulation (30s) — trigger a capacity fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized variant.
   - Script: "When capacity spikes, routing policy can failover to a compatible model variant and keep the feature live."
4) Quick cost/quality slide (30s) — show expected cost delta and a short QA: "How do we measure quality loss?"
5) Next steps ask (30s) — get commitment to run a 72-hour pilot dataset and nominate SE + Ops owner.

Rapid qualification checklist (pre-call):
- Does the prospect have PII/regulatory constraints? (yes -> Private/VPC path)
- Latency SLO target (p95) 
- Estimated peak concurrency and mean request size (tokens)
- Integration surface: REST API only or embedding + streaming?
- Decision criteria: throughput, error tolerance, cost per 1M tokens

Pilot setup quick steps (ops play):
1) Credentials: provision API key scoped to pilot project and generate a short-lived fallback key for canary failovers.
2) Model choice: default to a verified model in our catalog that matches the workload (note: prefer a quantized variant for cost-limited pilots).
3) Routing: set primary route to hosted-hosted-fast, fallback to quantized-variant in the same region.
4) Batching: configure small max batch (2–4) for latency-sensitive pilots; larger for throughput tests.
5) KV/prefix caching: enable for repeat prompt patterns (customer-specific).
6) Observability: turn on token-level retention for 72 hours, enable traces for a single customer route.

Canary & fallback checklist (must-read before demo):
- Canary percent: 10% traffic to new model variant for 1 hour -> watch latency and quality metrics.
- Auto-fallback threshold: deploy if p95 latency > target OR error rate > 1.5x baseline.
- Manual override: SE can flip route in Console; SRE will receive alert only after 3 sustained p95 breaches.
- Communicate to customer: expected downtime = 0 (graceful fallback), possible quality delta: small—include QA prompt set used for gating.

Cost talking points (short bullets):
- Unit economics: show delta between hosted standard and quantized variant as $ per 1k tokens (ballpark figures only in field doc).
- Predictability: Reserved pilot node provides predictable throughput pricing for pilot windows > 7 days.
- Quick hack: use prefix caching for demo to show cost drop by up to ~30% on repeat prompts.

Common objections + one-line responses (SE cheat lines):
- "We need strict quality guarantees." -> "We run a gated QA prompt set and enable canary rollouts; we’ll only escalate if the regression crosses your tolerance thresholds."
- "What about PII?" -> "We can run in Private/VPC with KMS integration and audit logs; pilot can be scoped to masked data."
- "How do we avoid surprise bills?" -> "We’ll set hard spend caps and per-route token quotas you control from the Console."

Failure modes & triage shortcuts (ops notes):
- Symptom: sudden p95 spike across all routes -> check region capacity and queue length; possible global GPU contention.
  - Quick action: enable fallback routing, increase batch timeout, trigger scale-up (if Dedicated).
- Symptom: quality regression on fallback -> revert routing, collect sample prompts, escalate to model onboarding team for variant tuning.
- Symptom: billing surge -> pause non-critical routes, enforce token cap, inform customer success.

Measurement & success criteria for 72-hour pilot (KPIs):
- Latency: p95 <= target (customer-defined) for >= 90% of test window
- Cost: average cost per 1k tokens within agreed range
- Availability: no >2 minute user-facing interruptions caused by runway failures
- Quality: QA prompt set pass rate >= agreed threshold (e.g., 90%)

Internal handoff template (to SE -> CS -> SRE):
- Pilot name, customer, contact, region, primary model, fallback model, quota caps, success criteria, monitoring links.
- Note: keep this in ticket JIRA-PILOT-142 and link to Confluence notes.

Notes to self / unresolved items (TODOs):
- Add quick price ranges per common models (low/med/high) — need updated pricing sheet from finance (ping Riley).
- Create a 1-minute animated GIF showing fallback toggle in Console for demos.
- Validate auto-fallback thresholds with SRE team — propose default p95 multiplier = 1.4.

Appendix (quick links for SEs):
- Console: https://console.redwood.ai/ (demo route: /pilot-demo)
- Pilot checklist board: confluence://GTMPilot/fastlane-notes
- Runbook snippets: confluence://SRE/runbooks/fallbacks

Speaker/owner notes: keep language crisp, avoid deep infra detail in initial demo, lean on measurable outcomes, ask for explicit pass/fail criteria before pilot starts.

---
End of compact draft. This is intentionally short — use as pocket reference during calls.
